title: Power Platform admin center: unified System Administrator user and role management for finance and operations apps
summary: Hold: the team automation targets Microsoft Entra group teams, which are not the Owner-type teams supported by this preview. The briefing also overstates who can grant System Administrator access: permission to assign some Dataverse roles does not permit assigning a more privileged role. The roadmap facts and most preview details are supported.

claims.quote: Administrators can now manage system administrator users and security roles for both finance and operations apps and Dataverse from a single, unified experience in Power Platform admin center.

claims.quote: admins can add and enable users, assign and remove roles, and review user access across both from one place.

claims.claim: Anyone who can assign roles in Dataverse can therefore grant administrator access to ERP data.
claims.quote: the person who is assigning the security role can't assign someone else to a security role that has more privileges than the assigner. For example, a CSR Manager can't assign another user to the System Administrator role.
claims.fix: Replace that sentence with: 'Anyone authorized to assign the Dataverse System Administrator role can therefore grant System Administrator access in finance and operations.' Permission to assign less privileged roles is not sufficient; keep the following privilege-elevation restriction and its existing citation.

claims.claim: The role-assignment procedure tells the reader to sign in as System Administrator.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Power Platform Admin center as a System Administrator. ... By default, the System Administrator security role has all the required privileges to assign security roles to any user, including assigning the System Administrator security role.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls prose and table
claims.claim: Learn does not say whether the Feature management data entity covers this feature.
claims.quote: A data entity with the name Feature management lets you export the Feature management settings from one environment and then import them into another environment. This entity updates only existing features.
claims.fix: Replace 'Learn does not say it covers this feature' and the matching prose caveat with: 'The data entity imports Feature management settings for existing features and applies the same rules as the Feature management workspace.' The preview page places this feature in that workspace; retain the existing reference.

claims.claim: The user-role path is Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Users > user > Manage security roles.
claims.quote: Select Users + permissions, and then select Users. ... On the Users page select a user, and then select Manage security roles. ... Select or deselect security roles.
claims.fix: The route reaches the correct role-management page. Complete it as 'Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Users > user > Manage security roles > security role' and clarify in the row note: 'These steps manage direct user role assignments; team-inherited roles are managed through the team.'

claims.claim: POST /api/data/v9.0/systemusers(azureactivedirectoryobjectid=<user object ID>)/systemuserroles_association/$ref assigns a security role to a user.
claims.quote:
POST [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.0/systemusers(azureactivedirectoryobjectid=<user object ID>)/systemuserroles_association/$ref
{ "@odata.id":"[Organization URI]/api/data/v9.0/roles(<role ID>)" }
claims.fix: Keep the printed call. Add to controls[1].note: 'The request body's @odata.id identifies the roles(<role ID>) record to assign.' The deterministic pre-check's missing-command lead is not confirmed: the exact endpoint is present in the cited reference.

claims.claim: The Owner-team role path is Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users and permissions > Teams > team > Manage security roles.
claims.quote: Select the three dots next to the team that has the System Administrator role. ... Select Manage security roles. ... Scroll to System Administrator and then check or clear the System Administrator selection.
claims.fix: Complete the path as 'Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users and permissions > Teams > team > Manage security roles > System Administrator'. Omitting the unlabelled three-dots button is not a blocker.

claims.claim: The Entra group-team alternate-key POST is the automation equivalent for assigning System Administrator to a supported Owner-type team.
claims.quote: A team can be one of the following types: Owner, Access, Microsoft Entra Security group, or Microsoft Entra Office group.
claims.fix: Replace controls[2].api.call with 'POST /api/data/v9.2/teams(<team ID>)/teamroles_association/$ref' and docs with https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/reference/team. Replace the group-team caveat in the note and prose with: 'Target the Dataverse ID of a Team type Owner team. The request body's @odata.id identifies the /api/data/v9.2/roles(<role ID>) record for System Administrator.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/associate-disassociate-entities-using-web-api for the collection POST and @odata.id syntax. The team reference read in this run documents /api/data/v9.2/teams, teamid, and the role-valued teamroles_association collection.

claims.claim: The printed teams(azureactivedirectoryobjectid=...,membershiptype=0)/teamroles_association/$ref call is documented for Microsoft Entra ID group teams.

Assign a security role to a Microsoft Entra ID group team
